title: Report Generation Flow
summary: Maps host and application report generation from persisted data through a shared ReportContext builder to a signed PDF.
coverage: How findings, occurrences, and metadata become report content
Host generate versus application sheet export

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Generated reports are built from data already saved in the database. Unsaved edits in the current browser session are not included in the PDF.

sections.title: Flow objective
paragraphs: RAPTOR keeps two generate endpoints that share one builder and one renderer. `POST /pentest/:id/generate-report` exports a single host. `POST /api/apps/:id/generate-report` exports an application, environment, or wave package (`owner_delivery`, `wave_archive`, `retest_pack`, `internal_draft`).

Both paths call `build_report_context` (host adapter or sheet builder), apply the org brand kit, then `render_pentest_report_pdf(context, template_definition)`. A record can still hold a manual uploaded PDF alongside the generated file.

sections.title: Generation prerequisites and gates
paragraphs: Report generation is permission-gated and record-gated. Host generate requires `export_pentests` plus owner, collaborator, or override. Application sheet export uses the same export permission on the app workspace. Wave packages can be generated while the wave is still open; ending a wave is a separate freeze and does not run as part of export.

sections.title: How report content is assembled
paragraphs: The builder produces a typed `ReportContext`: scope, package, application, environments, optional wave, hosts, findings with occurrence rows, and metrics. Occurrence-status counts use open-like and closed vocabularies. Findings never stringify hosts into the description field.

The renderer lints tokens, draws named cover / header / footer regions, and walks template blocks in order. Empty host-only blocks omit. Footer chrome is the RAPTOR lockup at the bottom-left, then company name and date. Brand kit print ink and logo override template hex wells at generate time. Severity and occurrence charts stay together on the page after overview, snapshot, and table of contents.

rows: Sheet exports pass `wave_id` / `env_ids` into findings fetch.

`vulnerabilities` block, severity chart, occurrence chart, metrics
Each finding lists occurrence DNS, environment, and status glyph, then Impact, Evidence, and Remediation as separate sections. `retest_pack` omits fixed occurrences.
`content_hash` and `signature` are stored on both host and sheet exports. They are not printed in the PDF footer.

sections.title: Operator sequence
paragraphs: Host reports are generated from the pentest record Overview tab. Application, environment, and wave packages are generated from the app workspace Export sheet. Confirm scope in the sheet; the sheet preview is a scope summary, not a second document.
orderedList: Save pentest or finding edits so the database holds the latest state.
Host track: choose a template under Generated Report, then Generate Report.
Sheet track: open Export sheet, choose package (`owner_delivery`, `wave_archive`, `retest_pack`, or `internal_draft`), environments or wave, and a template whose `supported_scopes` match.
Confirm the export scope, generate, then download. Classification lives on the cover; the footer is the RAPTOR lockup, company name, and date.
If output is stale, save again and regenerate. Generation always reads persisted state.

tip.title: TIP
paragraphs: The Settings paper preview swaps a frozen sample envelope (`host`, `env`, `wave`, and the four packages). It is not a live PDF of the current engagement.

sections.title: File lifecycle and replacement behavior
paragraphs: Generated and manual report files are stored separately. Regenerating replaces the generated artifact pointer and attempts cleanup of the previous generated file. Manual PDF upload updates the manual `report_file` pointer when the record is saved.

A host record can hold both files at the same time. Application sheet exports write `report_exports` rows with `package`, `content_hash`, and `signature`. Host generate writes the same HMAC columns with `package='host'`.
